I've been farming this land for 40 years. I know this soil, I know the weather here in Quzhou, and I know what works. My land is 6 mu, and every bit of it runs the same rotation — wheat in winter, maize in summer. That's how it's always been done here and it works well together.

**Wheat:** I plant in mid-October after the summer maize comes off. I'll use the Jimai or Kenong improved variety — not the old traditional seed, but also not some new hybrid I don't know yet. I've used improved wheat seed for over 20 years and the yields are reliable. For fertilizer, I apply compound fertilizer as base before planting, then urea topdressing when the wheat starts jointing in spring. I water three times: once before winter sets in to protect the roots, once at jointing, and once during grain fill. I spray herbicide once in early spring and then hit aphids and rust at heading. I use rotary tillage before planting — my plot is small enough and the soil needs it after the maize.

**Maize:** Right after I harvest the wheat in early June, I rotary till and plant maize. I always use hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, whichever I can get cheaper at the village supply station. I apply base fertilizer at planting and topdress with urea around the big bell stage. Summer rains usually help, but I pump water from the well twice — once at sowing if it's dry, once at silking because that's when missing rain really hurts yield. I spray once or twice — mostly for corn borer and leaf disease if I see it.

I'm not trying to maximize every last kilogram. I'm trying to keep costs reasonable and get a stable harvest. Two people in the household, 6 mu — we don't need to gamble.
